title: MCP client support: connect to external MCP servers
description:
Add MCP client capability to Scuffy. When configured, Scuffy connects to MCP servers at startup and registers their tools as native Scuffy tools.

Implementation:
1. npm install @modelcontextprotocol/sdk
2. New src/mcp/client.ts — connects to MCP server(s), discovers tools via listTools()
3. New src/mcp/bridge.ts — converts MCP tool definitions (JSON Schema) to Scuffy Tool objects (Zod + execute function that forwards calls to MCP server)
4. Config: SCUFFY_MCP_SERVERS env var or JSON config listing servers. Each entry has url and optional tools whitelist array. When tools is specified, only those tools are registered — critical for keeping context lean (agent mail has 40+ tools, we need ~4).
5. Wire into src/index.ts — at startup, connect to configured MCP servers, register bridged tools alongside native tools

Example config:
{"servers":[{"url":"http://localhost:8765/mcp","tools":["send_message","fetch_inbox","register_agent","mark_message_read"]}]}

~150-200 lines. MCP SDK handles the protocol; we just bridge tool formats and filter.

Acceptance criteria:
- Scuffy can connect to an MCP server (HTTP transport)
- Tool whitelist filters which tools get registered
- MCP tools appear in Scuffy's tool registry alongside native tools
- Scuffy can call MCP tools and get results
- Config supports multiple MCP servers
close_reason: MCP client support: connects to stdio/HTTP MCP servers at startup, bridges their tools into Scuffy's registry via SCUFFY_MCP_SERVERS env var

title: Fix stuck bead loop: skip in_progress beads that cannot advance
description:
bv --robot-next keeps returning ship-1kh (in_progress) but Scuffy cannot satisfy its acceptance criteria. Scuffy works on other beads instead but 1kh stays claimed forever, hogging the top pick slot.

Fix options (pick one):
A) Change headless system prompt: if bv --robot-next returns a bead that is already in_progress AND was claimed by a previous session, skip it and pick the next ready bead from br ready instead.
B) Add a --skip-in-progress flag to the summoner that unclaims stale in_progress beads before spawning.
C) Have finishBead detect when closing a bead different from the one bv suggested and log a warning.

Simplest fix is probably A — update HEADLESS_SYSTEM_PROMPT in src/index.ts to say: if the top pick from bv --robot-next is already in_progress, check br ready for other work. If nothing else is ready, escalate.

Root cause: Scuffy chose in-memory storage instead of Prisma, so the schema bead (design relational schema) could not be satisfied. This is a valid architectural choice by Scuffy but the bead-picking logic needs to handle it.

title: Exit tools (finishBead/escalate) commit to host repo when headless runs from repo root
description:
## Problem

The finishBead and escalate tools both run git commit as part of their exit flow. They commit in whatever directory workingDir points to. In normal operation (summoner pointing workingDir at workspace/ship-rebuild/), this is correct — commits land in the rebuild workspace.

However, when headless mode is run from the Scuffy repo root (e.g., during testing or development), the exit tools commit to the Scuffy source branch. This was discovered during OpenAI integration testing: three junk commits landed on task/summoner-fixes from headless test invocations — two WIP escalation commits and one finishBead commit that wrote a BRIEF.md.

## How it happened

1. Ran headless tests from /Users/gjw/dev/scuffy (the repo root)
2. workingDir defaulted to process.cwd() — the Scuffy source repo
3. The system prompt told the agent to find and work on beads
4. The agent claimed beads, did work (or escalated), and the exit tools ran git add + git commit
5. Those commits landed on the current Scuffy source branch, polluting git history

## Root cause

The exit tools (finishBead, escalate) unconditionally commit to the git repo at workingDir. There is no guard ensuring workingDir is a rebuild workspace vs. the agent's own source repo.

## Impact

- Junk commits on development branches that need manual cleanup (squash/rebase)
- Beads getting claimed and "closed" against the wrong repo
- If unnoticed, polluted git history could confuse Chair or other agents

## Suggested fix options

A) Add a guard to finishBead/escalate: refuse to commit if workingDir is the Scuffy source repo (detect via package.json name === "scuffy" or a sentinel file).

B) Add a --dry-run or --no-commit flag to headless mode for testing, where exit tools log what they would do but skip git operations.

C) Both A and B — guard in production, dry-run for testing.
close_reason: Subsumed by sc-3so (sandbox profile) and sc-bpo (claimBead) — the two root causes are now tracked separately
